findings.title: apps/web/e2e/README.md still claims the mock 'enforces' the owner floor, a claim the lane's own fix round established as false
findings.evidence: The `journal-work-walk.spec.ts` coverage row reads: '…and #848: an owner presses Reactivate on the `egress_not_authorized` face and reaches migration 0211's door end to end (the banner converges to active and the press re-reads), a governed `no_consent` refusal rendered verbatim, and the mock's own owner-floor enforcement answering the database's CLR04'. This sentence was added in commit 726bcfdd and the README was touched again in the fix-round commit f4c8f554 (for an unrelated L01-S5 sentence) without correcting this line. But the fix round's own L01-S2 finding (docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/reports/wave1-lane01-fixround-1.md) reproduces and confirms: 'the mock answers CLR04 purely on `state.egressReactivateAnswer === "denied"` (an armed flag), never inspecting a caller' — i.e. there is no enforcement at all, only a simulated wire answer — and the fix round's own remedy was to RENAME the test from a literal-enforcement claim to 'a forced denial renders the database's own CLR04 owner-floor refusal' specifically to stop asserting enforcement. The independent recheck (wave1-lane01-recheck-1.json, L01-S2) verified this rename and the absence of any actual enforcement logic in journal-work-mock.mjs. The README is therefore a documented false claim about the state of the code, left uncorrected through two commits that touched the same file.
findings.rule_violated: AGENTS.md working-protocol rule 6, 'Claims need evidence': 'Any statement about the state of the world … must be backed by a checkable source … If you cannot point to a source, say "unverified" instead of asserting. No evidence, no claim.' Also WORK-ORDER.md rule 9 ('Docs in the same commits: the module README your change affects') — the README was edited twice in this lane without ever being made to match what the code actually does.
